themes_detail.label: Animal Abuse Crisis Spike
themes_detail.summary: Animal abuse complaints surged to 13 THIS WEEK—an 700% spike vs. the 8-week baseline of 1.6 weekly complaints—suggesting a potential outbreak of intentional animal harm or neglect in Belmont/East Tremont that demands urgent investigation.
evidence: 13 animal abuse complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score 8.07)
Concurrent spike in dead animal complaints: 9 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 7.57)
Animal in park complaints also elevated: 4 last week vs. 0.2 average (1500% spike, z-score 8.66)
reporting_angles: Interview ASPCA and local animal control about whether they've detected a coordinated pattern or are responding to specific incidents in parks or streets
Map the 13 complaints geographically—are they clustered in one neighborhood park or dispersed across the district?

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals Appearing Across District
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped to 9 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.8 per week (1100% increase, z-score 7.57), potentially indicating a public health hazard, wildlife disease outbreak, or sanitation failure worth investigating.
evidence: 9 dead animal complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 7.57, severity: high)
Part of broader animal-related crisis: abuse (13 complaints) and park animal incidents (4) also spiking simultaneously
May reflect underlying sanitation or pest control breakdown in parks/streets
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks and Department of Sanitation about response times and whether they've mobilized additional cleanup crews
Ask Public Health about whether dead animals could signal disease outbreak (rabies, avian flu, etc.) requiring community alert

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion in Belmont
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 16 TWO WEEKS AGO from a 1.2 weekly baseline—a 1180% surge (z-score 12.3)—indicating rapid deterioration of streetscapes that may signal gang activity, vandalism rings, or broken-windows decline.
evidence: 16 graffiti complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.2 weekly average (1180% spike, z-score 12.3, severity: high)
Highest z-score among all spikes, indicating most statistically severe anomaly
Timing suggests an acute event 2 weeks ago rather than gradual deterioration
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and local precinct about whether a specific crew is active; check for gang tagging patterns
Follow up with Sanitation about graffiti removal capacity and timeline—is the district's cleanup backlog preventing removal?

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 47 LAST WEEK from a 14.1 weekly baseline—a 233% spike (z-score 3.76)—suggesting pothole, sidewalk, or pavement failure accelerating across the district.
evidence: 47 street condition complaints last week vs. 14.1 weekly average (233% spike, z-score 3.76, severity: high)
Correlates with ongoing community board requests for 'other transportation infrastructure' improvements—signal that requests have been unmet
May reflect recent weather events or deferred DOT maintenance
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DOT about whether heavy rain/freeze cycles caused a spike in pothole reports; cross-check with weather data
Verify if this district has filed complaints about lack of preventive street maintenance and whether budget allocation is inadequate

themes_detail.label: Public Drinking Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drinking-in-public complaints surged to 3 LAST WEEK from a 0.2 weekly baseline—an 1100% spike (z-score 6.35)—potentially indicating open-air substance use or failure of enforcement in parks and streets.
evidence: 3 drinking complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35, severity: high)
Concurrent encampment spike (5 complaints 3 weeks ago, 400% spike): possible housing/homelessness link
May reflect neighborhood quality-of-life deterioration or reduced police presence
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD about whether they've deprioritized public drinking enforcement; check arrest data for the district
Connect with community board about whether Parks or Sanitation have observed increased street drinking in specific parks or corners
